French government pushes for mandatory helmets for electric scooters, struggles with bicycles
subhead: State authorities around the country are increasingly requiring electric scooter users to wear helmets. Cycling advocacy groups argue such a rule would be counterproductive and would not protect cyclists in most potentially fatal accidents.

title: Sweden's right wing struggles to make most of late rebound on eve of elections
subhead: After a campaign in which purchasing power, education and health care ended up taking precedence over the immigration and security issues championed by the right and the far right, the left-wing bloc now leads ahead of the Sunday vote.

title: 25 French jihadists held in Iraq appeal to EU human rights court for repatriation
subhead: The Islamic State group members had been quietly transferred from Syria to Iraq, where they could face the death penalty. Their lawyers say Paris's refusal to prosecute them in France undermines the rule of law and opens to arbitrary decisions by the authorities.

title: 'Céline Dion's arrival in Paris rekindles a sense of national unity in France'
subhead: Although France has not always welcomed her with open arms, the Québécois star now inspires admiration. The use of her songs, especially in cinema, reflects a kind of universality, writes essayist Valentin Grimaud, author of 'Céline Dion: Vestale' ('Céline Dion: Vestal Virgin').

Bayeux Tapestry draws flocks in London seeking story 'etched in memory'
subhead: The first visitors admired the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum on Thursday. The work is on loan from France to the United Kingdom until July 2027. Public interest reflects both the importance of William the Conqueror's accession to the English throne in the national story and the fascination of seeing a nearly 1,000-year-old tapestry.

title: The forgotten French prisoner of 9/11
subhead: Zacarias Moussaoui, who was sent to the US by Al-Qaeda to prepare attacks and was convicted of complicity in the September 11 attacks, has spent the past 20 years serving a life sentence without the possibility of parole in a high-security penitentiary in Colorado. His lawyer is requesting his transfer to France.

title: Céline Dion's Paris residency brings economic boost: 'When you're a fan, money is no object'
subhead: After six years away from the stage, the Québécois superstar begins a run of 26 concerts in Paris on Saturday. Hoteliers, restaurateurs and retailers hope to benefit from the influx of nearly 800,000 fans, both French and international. The windfall is estimated at between €500 million and €1 billion, but it comes at a climate cost.
